brief.subject: FTC targets imposters, health plan ads and price gaps
brief.headline: FTC Cracks Down on Imposter Scams, Misleading Health Plan Ads and Register Overcharges
brief.dek: Imposter sites removed, warning letters to health plan marketers during open enrollment, and a lawsuit over shelf-versus-register prices.
brief.lede: Imposter scams remain the top reported fraud category, and the FTC says it has taken down 19 websites pretending to be the agency itself.

sections.heading: Fake FTC sites taken down
bullets: 19 websites posing as the FTC have been removed, so a government-looking site is not proof it's real.
More than $80 million in consumer redress has come from enforcement since the Impersonation Rule took effect in 2024.
Imposter scams rank as the top reported fraud category, making them the scam most worth discussing with older relatives.

sections.heading: Health plan ads under scrutiny
bullets: 25 companies that market healthcare plans or sell sales leads got FTC warning letters as open enrollment runs.
The letters flag deceptive or unfair claims about plan terms, so check coverage details before signing up.
More letters will go out on a rolling basis, signaling the agency sees an ongoing problem this season.

sections.heading: Dollar General sued over prices
bullets: The FTC and 20 states sued Dollar General, alleging register prices routinely exceeded shelf tags and ads.
Regulators say the practice cost consumers millions of dollars, so comparing receipts to shelf prices can pay off.

sections.heading: Your data and the price you pay
bullets: Nine major airlines, ride-sharing and food-delivery firms must tell the FTC how personal data shapes prices and pay.
The study could reveal whether your personal information affects what you're charged for everyday services.

brief.seo_description: FTC removes 19 fake FTC websites, warns 25 health plan marketers during open enrollment, and sues Dollar General over register overcharges.
